learning_outcomes.text: Prepare students for the gradual but ceaseless advent of nanotechnology and its related techniques in science, technology and practice.
Give students a concept of what nanotechnology is and what it constitutes.
Teach how to produce and measure nanotechnology.
Provide knowledge on when nanotechnology can be expected to be used in engineering practice.

syllabus_topics: Course Introduction, foundations of physics of nanomaterials, atomic shell electron structure, and atomic bond in compounds
Basic crystallographic structure of materials, crystal surfaces and their marking, symmetry, surface characteristics.
Basic principles of STM and AFM, other types of microscope techniques and their possible using.
Formation of nanoparticles, nanowires and two-dimensional nanostructures, methods of MBE, MOVPE, BUT, LB.
Photo and X-ray lithography, lithography of focus ion beam, nanomanipulation.
Nanomaterials based on carbon - fullerenes, nanotubes, nanodiamond, their production and application.
Properties and applications of the most common nanomaterials: polymorphic modifications of TiO2. Photocatalysis in environmental protection. Ag, Au, ZnO, Fe0.
Nanocomposites, their production, properties and uses.
The use of micromechanical structures in science and engineering practice, the design and production methods.
The use of nanostructures and nanomaterials in bio-applications and treatments.
Health risks of nanotechnology, the principles of safety and usage.
Review of the current state of nanotechnology in practice.
Overview of future trends of science and technology with the use of nanotechnology.
Summarizing lecture and preparation for the exam.
bibliography: Hošek J. Úvod do nanotechnologie, Skripta ČVUT, 2010
Nanotechnology: A Gentle Introduction to the Next Big Idea by Mark A Ratner, Daniel Ratner
Nanotechnology: Basic Science and Emerging Technologies by Carol Crane, Michael Wilson, Kamali Kannangara, Geoff Smith, Wilson Wilson
Introduction to Nanotechnology, by Charles P. Poole, Frank J. Owens
